FAILED tests/llm/accuracy_conformance.py::test_accuracy_conformance[TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0-INT8-GPU] - TypeError: genai_gen_text() got an unexpected keyword argument 'context'

root_cause: tests/llm/accuracy_conformance.py imports `genai_gen_text` from `whowhatbench.wwb` and passes it as `gen_answer_fn` to `wwb.Evaluator(...)`; whowhatbench's internal `text_evaluator.py::_generate_data` (line 236) invokes `gen_answer_fn(..., context=...)`. The `whowhatbench` package is installed unpinned, straight from `git+https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino.genai.git#subdirectory=tools/who_what_benchmark` (tests/llm/requirements.txt) with no ref/tag, so every CI run resolves the current HEAD of the openvino.genai repository's `master` branch. A recent upstream change there altered `genai_gen_text`'s signature (dropped/renamed the `context` parameter) without a matching update to `_generate_data`'s call site, or the reverse: `_generate_data` started passing `context` while `genai_gen_text` was not updated to accept it. Either way this is an uncoordinated breaking change between two co-evolving parts of the same upstream package resolved at HEAD, surfacing identically on both CPU and GPU jobs for all 4 model/precision combinations (deterministic, 100% reproduction). The triggering PR #39512 only edits a benchmarks CSV file and is unrelated to this failure; the merge queue simply hit a broken state of the `whowhatbench` git dependency at build time.
reproduction_steps:
1. `pip install "whowhatbench[llm-test-openvino] @ git+https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino.genai.git#subdirectory=tools/who_what_benchmark"` (no ref pin; picks up current master HEAD).
2. Run `python3 -m pytest tests/llm/accuracy_conformance.py -k CPU --tb native` on a workspace with `tests/llm/accuracy_conformance.py` as in this repo.
3. Observe `TypeError: genai_gen_text() got an unexpected keyword argument 'context'` for every parametrized test case.
recommended_actions: Pin `whowhatbench` in tests/llm/requirements.txt to a known-good commit/tag of openvino.genai instead of an unqualified git URL, so this repo's test code and the whowhatbench package version are co-versioned.

Inspect the current `whowhatbench/text_evaluator.py::_generate_data` and `whowhatbench/wwb.py::genai_gen_text` signatures on openvino.genai master to determine which side changed, and either update the pin to a commit before the breaking change or update `tests/llm/accuracy_conformance.py` usage to match the new `genai_gen_text` signature.

Add a CI smoke check that fails fast (e.g., `python -c 'import inspect; ...'`) when the whowhatbench API surface used by accuracy_conformance.py changes, to catch this class of break before the full (slow) accuracy suite runs.
prevention_strategies: Avoid unpinned git dependencies for test-only packages that are developed in lockstep with test code living in a different repository; pin to a tag/commit and bump deliberately via a PR that also updates call sites. Add a lightweight contract/signature check between tests/llm/accuracy_conformance.py and the whowhatbench API it depends on.
